look_here_first: Find the low, radiating mat with opposite, uneven-based leaves. Check a leaf: usually 4–18 mm long, finely toothed and hairy, often with a red midrib blotch (the blotch is NOT required). Next inspect the tiny axillary cyathia and a mature 3-lobed capsule under magnification. In spotted spurge the capsule is hairy across its faces, and the seed has lengthwise rounded ridges; do not identify from the dark leaf spot alone.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual with a taproot; stems usually lie flat and do not root at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, asymmetric at base, 4–18 × 2.5–8 mm, often red-blotched but variable.
morphology_keys.reproductive: Tiny cup-shaped cyathia in leaf axils; hairy 3-lobed capsules and longitudinally ridged seeds are stronger tie-breakers than leaf color.
best_field_traits: Opposite leaves with strongly unequal bases
Hairy capsule faces and lengthwise ridges on mature seeds

comparisons.key_distinctions: Euphorbia prostrata: may also be hairy and mat-forming, but has more symmetrical leaf bases, capsule hairs concentrated along the keels, and seed surface with crosswise ridges or wrinkles rather than the rounded lengthwise ridges of E. maculata. Euphorbia serpens: smaller rounder, usually smooth leaves and stems that root at nodes. Dark leaf spots alone are unreliable.
comparisons.photo_tie_breakers: Request macros of leaf base, capsule surface and seed with scale; the existing single photo is not verified to show these structures.
